主要内容: On December 8, 2017, Nasdaq announced the annual re-ranking of the NASDAQ-100 Index, which will take effect before the market opens on December 18, 2017. Five companies were added to the index: ASML Holding N.V. (ASML), Cadence Design Systems, Inc. (CDNS), Synopsys, Inc. (SNPS), Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (TTWO), and Workday, Inc. (WDAY). Six companies were removed: Akamai Technologies, Inc. (AKAM), Discovery Communications Series A (DISCA), Discovery Communications Series C (DISCK), Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. (NCLH), Tractor Supply Company (TSCO), and Viacom Inc. (VIAB). The NASDAQ-100 Index, composed of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on NASDAQ, has returned over 3,731% since its inception in 1985. It serves as a benchmark for financial products such as options, futures, and funds. The re-ranking is timed with the quadruple witching expiration, and the index is the basis for the PowerShares QQQ Trust (QQQ). The NASDAQ-100 Index undergoes annual changes, reflecting the evolving landscape of the technology and financial sectors. The index includes companies such as ASML Holding N.V., Cadence Design Systems, Inc., Synopsys, Inc., Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., and Workday, which are key players in semiconductor equipment, electronic design automation, software development, and interactive entertainment. These companies are significant contributors to the NASDAQ-100 Index, which is a benchmark for the technology sector. The NASDAQ-100 Index is home to approximately 3,900 total listings with a market value of approximately $12 trillion. Securities explicitly mentioned in the source include Nasdaq (NDAQ), NDX.
